page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e3.small is an entry-level instance configured with 1 vCPU and 8.0 GB of memory, delivering a high 1:8 core-to-RAM ratio. Built on x86_64 architecture and running on a KVM hypervisor, the instance utilizes an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The single virtual processor maps to one dedicated physical core with a single thread, supported by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 35 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512, and AES-NI. The instance includes no bundled local storage and provision zero integrated GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached block storage for persistence.

Benchmark evaluations place the instance in the lower performance brackets due to its single-thread limitations. The server achieved 1015.38 in both single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests, alongside a Geekbench single-core score of 939.0 and multi-core score of 937.0. Memory throughput yields 8.76 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 7.12 GB/sec for writes, scaling to 80.64 GB/sec for cached 16 KB operations. In application-focused metrics, it sustained 1.31 million operations per second in Redis SET routines and 1.27 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. These metrics highlight moderate I/O and computing thresholds bounded by the single compute core.

The hardware configuration provides favorable resource economics for scenarios demanding modest compute alongside larger working memory. Because compute overhead is restricted to a single execution thread, the machine is not suited for parallel compilation, heavy batch processing, or compute-heavy analytics. Instead, Alibaba Cloud ecs.e3.small is best fitted for small in-memory key-value stores, staging databases, lightweight microservices, and development environments requiring an 8 GB memory footprint without paying for surplus CPU cores.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e3.small is an entry-tier virtual instance featuring 1 dedicated vCPU powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor at 2.5 GHz and 8.0 GB of RAM. Operating under KVM virtualization on x86_64 architecture, it provides an elevated 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio without bundled local storage or GPU hardware. Benchmark results reflect single-core compute performance, scoring 1015.38 in stress-ng and 939.0 in Geekbench single-core evaluations. Memory operations deliver 8.76 GB/sec in uncached block reads, supporting up to 1.31 million Redis SET operations per second and 1.27 GB/sec in static web throughput. Due to its dedicated single-thread execution and expanded memory footprint, the instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-centric, low-compute workloads such as small caching layers, background task queues, and low-traffic web applications.
